title: Young people freer now: ballroom age rules and halls
summary: Wilson says people had a better time in the old days; 21 to enter ballrooms, chaperoned girls at Economy Hall, and his own gambling and not drinking.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. No, they had a better time in all of these. There's more places to go now than it was then. Because when I was a young man, you had to be 21 years old to go in the ballroom. You couldn't go there and fool the man, the owner, the place, the bartender, you tell him you're 21. You couldn't lie in them. Not anything goes in the ballroom. Well, they come along and say, how old are you? I'm 18 or 19. Go ahead. But we couldn't get by with that kind of stuff. No, we couldn't get by with that. I was 18 years old. I couldn't look in the ballroom. But today, there's so many places. Like my little brother, he's just 17 years old. Go to all them places. I couldn't go in them. The young people is more free now than they was in the olden days. Now they had a hall around here. We call it a corporate hall. And the economy hall. Now if a young girl would go to a dance, she went with some of her parents. It had to be her brother, her uncle, her mother, her sister, her aunt. And that certain amount of hours was, say, 11 o'clock, 11.30, they had to leave. They left. They went home. Then the sporting class of people would come on. They'd come on. They'd always break up at two o'clock in the morning, sometimes four in the morning. Well, they just mixed like they do now. Everybody's together now. But in those times in certain classes, you bump by yourself, I bump by myself. And we had a bunch of men on that corner over there. When a younger man bumped on his corner, he didn't bump the older man. Didn't drink with him. He wasn't asking for a match. We didn't allow it. But I was a young fella. And I went out in that Orange Channel. And I was a man before guys even knew I drank. They tried all kinds of ways. And I used to gamble. We'd catch that slack poker. And they'd allow me to gamble with them. And they'd buy a dress and offer a drink, but I never drink. And I used to put these within a, I ain't gonna make that fella drunk. He didn't know myself, you ain't gonna make this fella drunk. A long time before I started drinking. And now I don't drink much now. I'll drink a few beers. I never go out through the week unless it's something important, a meeting, something like that. When I come from down there around this time of the, I was digging here, I sat out there while I got television in the back. I went in here, I got a radio back there. That dogma thing, I don't know when I played that thing, that music box.
